title: McLaren agrees settlement with Chip Ganassi Racing over Alex Palou’s contract breach
content:
McLaren has reached a settlement with Chip Ganassi Racing over IndyCar champion Alex Palou’s contractual breach following a UK court ruling in January.

McLaren won the case it brought against Palou following his decision to renege on his agreement to join its IndyCar team in 2023. Palou had initially signed to race for McLaren in IndyCar alongside a role as its F1 reserve driver, believing there was a pathway to move into an F1 race seat in the future.

After Palou opted to remain with his existing team, Chip Ganassi Racing, beyond 2023, McLaren sued Palou for around $20million in losses, leading to a trial at London’s High Court late last year.

Justice Simon Picken detailed in his judgement that McLaren should be awarded an initial $10.2m, increasing to between $12.2m and $12.7m to be added depending on the outcome of expert evidence.

Following the ruling in McLaren’s favor, Palou said in a statement he was “disappointed that any damages have been awarded to McLaren,” and he was “considering my options with my advisors.”

But on Friday, Palou, Chip Ganassi Racing and McLaren all issued statements confirming that a settlement had now been reached, bringing the matter to an end.

The statements did not disclose the terms of the settlement. When contacted by The Athletic, both McLaren and Chip Ganassi Racing declined to provide any further comment.

“I’m happy to confirm that we have reached a final settlement with McLaren Racing following a UK judge ruling in January,” said Chip Ganassi, the founder of his eponymous team, in a statement.

“I cannot condone what happened and I’m glad that the matter is over. With the benefit of hindsight, I hope Alex has learned it’s important to keep good people around him, which he now does, so the events of 2023 are never repeated.

“I want to thank Zak (Brown, McLaren Racing’s CEO) and McLaren Racing for now giving us a chance to leave this matter behind us and fully focus on the exciting IndyCar season ahead.”

In his own statement issued by McLaren, Brown said: “I’m very pleased that we have reached a final settlement with Chip Ganassi Racing after a UK judge ruled in our favor in January.

“I want to thank the team working directly on the case for so many months, and everyone who supported us throughout the process. I’m pleased we can now return to battling things out on track and focus on what’s set to be an exciting IndyCar season.”

During the trial, Palou’s legal team argued that McLaren’s claim had been “vastly overinflated” and that no damages were payable, with Palou claiming his decision to go back on his contract was “based on lies and false impressions” about a possible F1 opportunity.

The Spanish driver ultimately remained with Chip Ganassi Racing beyond 2023, having initially been due to join McLaren for 2024, and has won the last three IndyCar championships. Palou also won last year’s Indianapolis 500.

Palou expressed regret in his statement on Friday, acknowledging that both Brown and Ganassi were “put in a difficult position, and I regret being in the middle of that,” and that what happened in 2023 “could have been handled differently.”

Palou continued: “While little of this is publicly known, I found myself pulled in various directions.

“In hindsight, had I reached out to Zak directly, perhaps things may have played out differently.

“McLaren and Zak supported me in many ways, they fulfilled every obligation, went above and beyond and delivered on everything they said in their contracts. I was never misled by McLaren and I very much respect their organization.”

Palou added he was “delighted the matter has now settled” and that he looked forward to the sole competition between McLaren and Chip Ganassi Racing taking place on the track.

The new IndyCar season will begin on Sunday with the Grand Prix of St. Petersburg.
